title: The Creator wrapped in swaddling clothes and laid in a manger

edition.locus: Vossius 1684 Opera omnia, Latin column, In annuntiationem Sermo I, printed p. 14, cols. B-C (PDF p. 38)

source_text: Fasciis eum involuit, qui amictus est lumine sicut vestimento. Involuit pannis eum, qui omnem formavit creaturam. Reclinavit in praesepio eum, qui super cherubim sedet, et ab infinitis Angelis collaudatur. In irrationalium animalium praesepio divinum requievit Verbum, ut hominibus vere irrationalibus secundum liberam voluntatem, rationalem sensum tribueret. In mensa iumentorum, caelestis panis propositus est: ut homines instar pecorum irrationales, mystici cibi participes redderet.
pass_a_gloss: With swaddling bands (fasciae) she wrapped Him, who is clothed (amictus est) with light (lumen) as with a garment (vestimentum). She wrapped Him in cloths (panni), who formed (formavit) all creation (creatura). She laid in a manger Him, who sits (sedet) above the cherubim, and by infinite Angels (infiniti Angeli) is praised (collaudatur). In the manger of irrational animals (irrationalia animalia) the divine Word rested (requievit), that to men truly irrational (vere irrationales) according to free will (secundum liberam voluntatem), rational sense (rationalis sensus) He might give (tribueret). On the table of beasts of burden (mensa iumentorum), heavenly bread (caelestis panis) was set forth (propositus est): that men like cattle (instar pecorum) irrational, sharers (participes) of mystical food (mysticus cibus) it/He might render (redderet).

choices.choice: The wordplay irrationalis / rationalis is kept as 'without reason' / 'a sense of reason'.
'caelestis panis' may recall John 6:51 and 'instar pecorum' Psalm 49:12 (Vulgate 48:13); uncertain, not cited.
Margin variant 'al. panis vitae appositus est' not adopted.

pass_b_english: She swathed in swaddling bands Him who clothes Himself with light as with a garment (Psalm 104:2). She wrapped in cloths Him who formed all creation. She laid in a manger Him who sits above the cherubim (Psalm 80:1) and is praised by countless angels (Daniel 7:10). In the manger of beasts without reason the divine Word rested, to give a sense of reason to men who were truly without reason by their own free will. On the table of beasts of burden the heavenly bread was set out, to make men, who were without reason like cattle, sharers in the mystical food.
notes: Margins 'Psal. 103' and 'Psal. 79' are Vulgate numbering: Vulgate Psalm 103:2 = Psalm 104:2 and Vulgate Psalm 79:2 = Psalm 80:1 in English Bibles; English numbering cited. Margin 'Dan. 7': Daniel 7:10 (thousands upon thousands serving Him). 'Fasciis eum' read for the print's 'Fasciis cum' (misprint; see source note). The wordplay irrationalis / rationalis is kept as 'without reason' / 'a sense of reason'. 'redderet' has no expressed subject (the Word or the bread, which here is Christ); an infinitive of purpose ('to make') keeps that open. 'caelestis panis' may recall John 6:51 and 'instar pecorum' Psalm 49:12 (Vulgate 48:13); uncertain, not cited. Margin variant 'al. panis vitae appositus est' not adopted.
source_notes: PDF p. 38 = printed p. 14, cols. B-C. Margins 'Psal. 103' (Vulgate = Psalm 104:2), 'Psal. 79' (Vulgate = Psalm 80:1), 'Dan. 7' (Daniel 7:10). 'Fasciis eum': the print (and the OCR) reads 'Fasciis cum', an evident misprint for 'eum' (the object is required and the next two sentences repeat 'eum'); corrected here. Margin at 'caelestis panis propositus est': 'al. panis vitae appositus est'.
